quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous for motorcycle riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many accidents happen there. Motorcyclists and other drivers may have conflicts at intersections.

questions.question: A person over 21 with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In New Mexico, you can be arrested for driving with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in cities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you better.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. If you speed up, they may just tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it can be done before another vehicle arrives.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the road.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system. Even one drink per hour can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see far to the sides as needed.
Does not have any markings or labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels showing the maker's name and the safety standards they meet.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only if you will carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It should only take a few minutes.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not ask the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Do not carry a passenger unless your motorcycle has a large enough seat for two riders. Your motorcycle should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you.

questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover your ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on things. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on motorcycle parts.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you faster, which increases danger.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do with your feet?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes downward, as your toes may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same way as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be operated in curves.
It should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. These signs tell you the driving rules you must follow.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects the eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the most protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough protection. Face shields are recommended but not always required by law.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete.
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Dry concrete is not slippery and provides good tire grip.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer to stop than usual, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead when on slippery surfaces. This gives you more time and space to stop safely.

questions.question: What helmet gives the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has been in a crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the most protection. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to easily reach and operate all the controls.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: As much as a face shield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your face. A face shield protects your whole face and is recommended over goggles. A windshield alone is not adequate protection.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:
questions.correctAnswerText: Are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy. They should cover and support your ankles. The soles must be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Switching to a lower gear is also called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows your motorcycle like brakes do. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can make it unsafe to ride. When mixed with alcohol, these medications become even more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle and changes how it handles. Your motorcycle will speed up, turn, and stop more slowly than usual. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps before crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, you should check all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Damage to the paint.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and turn signals. Paint damage is not a safety check.
